Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 30-year-old woman with 7-day history of fever, alternating chills/hot sweats, generalized myalgias, nausea, and fatigue.  
• Returned from rural Vietnam 4 weeks ago; took daily but unspecified malaria prophylaxis; extensive outdoor exposure.  
• No localizing infectious focus on review of systems; no rash, cough, urinary or gastrointestinal symptoms.  

Working diagnosis  
• Undifferentiated febrile illness—high suspicion for malaria (supported by travel history and symptom pattern).  

Supporting differentials (consistent with DDx)  
1. Malaria – High likelihood; classic presentation post-travel despite prophylaxis.  
2. Acute systemic viral illness (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) – Medium likelihood; compatible symptoms but duration and lack of respiratory features lessen probability.  
3. Dengue/other arboviral infection – Medium-low likelihood; endemic region exposure but incubation timing and absent rash/arthralgia reduce probability.  

Management/Referral Plan  
• Arrange urgent in-person examination at clinic today.  
• Order blood work: thick & thin blood films for malaria, full blood count, inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR), liver and renal panels, electrolytes, blood cultures, viral PCR as indicated.  
• Consider malaria rapid diagnostic test if available.  
• Advise patient not to attend work until assessment complete.  
• If clinic attendance delayed, patient to attend nearest emergency department with copy of plan.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Malaria – High: Returned from endemic area; fever with alternating chills/sweats and myalgias despite prophylaxis.  
2. Acute systemic viral infection (influenza/COVID-19) – Medium: Common cause of febrile myalgias without focus, but persistent high fever after 7 days and minimal respiratory symptoms lower likelihood.  
3. Dengue or other arboviral infection – Medium-Low: Rural SE-Asia exposure; fever and myalgias; incubation period slightly long and absent typical rash/arthralgia.
